beforeImage.name: Braya Renewable Fuels
beforeImage.subsector: Renewable diesel and low-carbon fuels refining
beforeImage.description: Braya Renewable Fuels owns the Come By Chance refinery complex in Newfoundland and Labrador and is converting and operating the site for renewable and low-carbon fuel production. Its customer base is tied to fuel markets and distributors, with economics influenced by physical refining margins and low-carbon fuel programs rather than regulated utility-style revenues. The platform is highly asset-heavy, centered on a large existing refinery and associated logistics infrastructure that has been repurposed for renewable diesel production. Energy Capital Partners announced a $300 million investment in 2023, and Braya said in early 2024 that the facility had commenced commercial operations for renewable fuel production. Newfoundland and Labrador government materials in 2025 identified the ownership group as including Cresta Fund Management, North Atlantic Refining Corp. managed by Silverpeak, and Energy Capital Partners.

milestones.event: The Come By Chance refinery changed ownership and began repositioning toward renewable fuels.
ECP announced a $300 million preferred equity investment in Braya Renewable Fuels.
Braya announced commencement of commercial operations.

afterImage.name: Braya Renewable Fuels
afterImage.subsector: Renewable diesel and low-carbon fuels refining
afterImage.description: Braya Renewable Fuels is the manager-level renewable-fuels platform operating the Come By Chance refinery in Newfoundland and Labrador through Braya Renewable Fuels (Newfoundland) LP. Cresta Fund Management acquired control in November 2021, while Silverpeak-managed North Atlantic Refining Corp. retained a minority interest. ECP announced a US$300 million preferred-equity investment in April 2023. Exact sponsor percentages, voting rights and holding vehicles are not publicly disclosed, and ECP Fund V is not directly supported for this investment. Commercial renewable-diesel operations began in February 2024; after a temporary 2025 shutdown, operations resumed, and the platform announced its first 100,000-barrel Canadian renewable-diesel sale in June 2026. Braya serves fuel markets in Canada, the United States, Mexico and Europe, while sustainable aviation fuel and green hydrogen or ammonia remain planned rather than confirmed commercial products. No later sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.
